Weekend rules for the early crew
This section explains the steps that matter
Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: keep animal travel requests moving without delay and without error.

Staff must confirm the booking file first, then check the animal category, carrier condition, and customer notes before any promise is made. Use clear, respectful language, record each change in the desk ledger at once, and keep the traveler informed when a file needs review. When a case concerns a rabbit, <<FACT F064>> and the record must show that the condition was checked before acceptance. Do not guess, do not improvise, and do not release incomplete guidance to the customer.

For birds, the health certificate must be reviewed as a live document, and the desk must reject any file with unclear handwriting, missing stamps, or a mismatch between the certificate and the reservation. <<FACT F083>> If the airline system or station note conflicts with the paper file, pause the case and escalate it through the senior coordinator. Under no circumstance is a clerk to bypass the review path or approve travel on the basis of verbal assurance alone.

Rabbit travel remains tightly controlled, and every request must be screened for age, fitness, and carrier suitability before the case moves forward. <<FACT F076>> If the animal is too young, the answer is a firm no, and the file stays open only for referral and follow-up. Staff must not send mixed messages, and any correction to a prior note must be entered in the ledger immediately.

Where a traveler such as Andre Martin or Eva Kowalski presents incomplete papers, respond with calm firmness, request the missing items, and advise that the desk cannot proceed until the record is complete. If Olive or any other pet appears in the manifest with conflicting details, hold the case, notify the supervisor, and wait for instruction. Escalations must follow a stepwise review, with each decision documented, because speed matters only when accuracy is preserved.

For urgent exceptions, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at once.
